thread:
IncidentBot: [PAGER] sev2: Dedicated pool 'apexcore-prod-vpc' GPU utilization >95% for 3m, requests queuing. Paging on-call.
Olivia Oncall: I'm on it, paging SREs and infra. @Dennis can you join? :phone:
Dennis SRE: here, looking at queue lengths and jobs. seeing sustained spike from tenant apexcore, ~420 pending tasks across GPUs.
Maya Product: Jackie CS just flagged customer chat - ApexCore is seeing increased latencies in production endpoints, reporting timeouts.
Jackie CS: confirmed, customer reports 5-10% error rate on generation calls. They want ETA, asking if we can burst now.
Carlos Eng: quick check: dedicated pool autoscale policy is at max_reserved and burst is enabled but subject to billing/approval. current pool size 32 GPUs, node provisioning slow (~4-6m).
Liam Infra: I can trigger emergency burst override for dedicated pools but need approval from product or oncall lead. Risk: we may violate reserved capacity commit and escalate billing.
Olivia Oncall: assess customer impact first - is ApexCore degraded below SLO? Dennis?
Dennis SRE: P95 latency for ApexCore routes jumped from 120ms -> 2.4s, error rate 7% over last 10m. Gateway 503s correlated to queue overflow on model servers.
Nina Support: Jackie relaying to customer that we're investigating, keeping them updated every 10m.
Maya Product: ApexCore is enterprise tier with SLA. Recommend temporary burst. I'll OK billing hit for immediate customer impact mitigation.
Carlos Eng: cool - if Product approves, Infra can initiate burst. Steps: 1) enable burst override (infra console) 2) provision 8 extra GPU nodes 3) route tenant traffic gradually to new capacity.
Liam Infra: starting override now. command: `infra burst override --pool apexcore-prod-vpc --force --scale 8` will take ~5m. monitoring health.
IncidentBot: action logged by Olivia Oncall: burst_override initiated by Liam Infra.
Dennis SRE: creating a shortblock to prevent eviction thrashing: set tenant weight to high for routing, pause non-critical background jobs for this tenant.
Carlos Eng: pausing scheduled model snapshots for ApexCore and lowering batch sizes for internal backfills.
Olivia Oncall: Jackie please tell customer: we approved a short burst to restore service, ETA ~7-10m for visible improvement.
Jackie CS: message sent to ApexCore: "We've initiated emergency capacity to reduce errors - we'll update in 10 minutes. Apologies for the disruption."
Liam Infra: nodes coming up, 6/8 ready, kube pull complete, models warming. KV cache warming in progress.
Dennis SRE: queue length falling from 420 -> 80, error rate down to 1.5%, p95 latency 360ms and trending down.
Maya Product: good. We'll keep burst for 30m, monitor for regen of load. If traffic persists, propose scheduled scaling change + cost review.
Olivia Oncall: logging timeline and postmortem owner. Dennis will follow up with root cause investigation and propose permanent mitigations.
Dennis SRE: noted. immediate next steps: collect traces, correlate request payload sizes, check if any noisy tenant jobs caused burst.
Carlos Eng: provisional mitigations: stricter tenant rate limits, dynamic KV-cache sizing, and an autoscale policy tweak to allow faster provisioning.
Jackie CS: ApexCore replied: "Thanks - service improving. Please keep us posted on root cause and any config changes that could impact latency."
Nina Support: scheduling a 1:1 with the customer tomorrow to go over the incident and mitigations.
Olivia Oncall: incident status -> mitigated. Keeping channel open for any regressions. Postmortem draft assigned to Dennis SRE with input from Carlos and Liam.
IncidentBot: Incident closed for paging but thread open for follow-ups.
